failure_summary: render_decision.requiredSet lists only opp-major/opp-major-line/better-col, so the offered opp-fork-pivot alias (spec c5r3 — the square X plays to make the stacked figure_7 live) is never obliged and no run names it, even though the punishment line 315233253621552234626653644 shows X playing c5r3 to turn c5r4 into a gravity-top four with c5r5 behind it; the pivot's coordinate is also absent from the assembled prompt (PROMPT.includes('c5r3') === false), so this is model-independent.
notes: n_runs=3, not 5 — the run file contains only run_index 0-2 for this id/condition; mechanical keys |D|3 and |D|4 are absent, as expected. A1/A2/A6/G7a_offered/G7b_offered copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_v3retry63_2026-09-01T20-55-54Z_mechanical.json (all pass). Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 null (not scored, not passed). A5/A7/G1/G3/G6/G7 graded on all 3 runs, all against servedExplanation with [zone:]/[term:] markup stripped per the v2 addendum. A7e: N/A — trigger does not fire. On the after-played board 31523325362155223462665364 the played disc lands at c5r2, col5 height becomes 2, and both opponent majors (c5r4, c5r5) stay NON-gravity-top ([X], no [GT] in visualize_board.sh); production detectImmediateThreat(new Board('31523325362155223462665364'), 1) returns {matched:false,cells:[]}. Consistent with the v3 addendum's measured list, which names pin-branch-invariance-true-2 and -3 but not -1. A7c (runs 0,1,2): the mechanism is a fork — opponentPunishment.tag='figure_7' and the render's own link.text says 'Your opponent's 7-shaped double threat in column 5' — and render_decision.zones.aliases DOES offer opp-fork-pivot (spec c5r3, role 'the square your opponent plays to CREATE the fork'), so the pivot check applies. No run names or wraps it; runs 0-2 name only the single finishing square c5r4 and the diagonal line c4r5-c5r4-c6r3-c7r2, never the second finishing square c5r5 nor the creating square c5r3. A player told only 'the key square at column 5, row 4' would block c5r4 and lose to c5r5. A7b (run 2 only): 'the same [zone:windows:c7r2,c6r3,c5r4,c4r5]four-in-a-row line from column 4 to column 7 on row 5[/zone:...]' — the words name the HORIZONTAL row-5 line (which is a real second opponent threat, offered separately as opp-major-line-2, spec windows:c4r5,c5r5,c6r5,c7r5) while the emitted handle lights up the DIAGONAL; the same sentence then calls 'the lower square in column 5' (c5r4) the key point of that line, and c5r4 is not on row 5 at all, so the referent does not resolve. G7 (run 2 only): same defect on the judgment half — the opp-major-line handle wraps a phrase whose meaning is the other line, contradicting its own role text ('the diagonal line falling from column 4 on row 5 to column 7 on row 2'); annotationRepairs is [] on all 3 runs. G2 (runs 0-1): the L3 guardrail is honored — no run says the played move caused/enabled the pattern, all frame column 1 as the toughest defense, and none appends a defeatist caveat. G4/G5 (runs 0-1): every named cell/line is true on render_decision.finalMovestring 315233253621552234626653644 (c4r5, c6r3, c7r2 are X, c5r4 empty and gravity-top there), and both rendered threat-list entries ('major at c5r4 (opp)', 'major at c5r5 (opp)') are board-true on the decision board. G6: patternOnAfterBestBoard=true is correct — the after-best board 31523325362155223462665360 still shows both col5 majors — so the L3 route is right. Retry note: runs 1 and 2 fired a retry with reason missingHandles=['better-col']; the graded post-retry answers do carry better-col.
